answer:
The adapter adds (alpha/rank)·BA to the frozen weight. A is random and B starts at zero, so the initial model exactly matches the base while B can receive gradients. Only adapter parameters should enter the optimizer. merge_weights returns a separate frozen Linear containing the combined weight and original bias; calling it twice cannot accidentally double the update. This API deliberately treats the merged layer as an inference artifact.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** The update is $W'=W+(\alpha/r)BA$ with $A\in\mathbb R^{r\times d_{in}}$ and $B\in\mathbb R^{d_{out}\times r}$. Trainable weight count becomes $r(d_{in}+d_{out})$ instead of $d_{in}d_{out}$. At initialization $B=0$ makes the update zero, while gradients can first reach $B$ through nonzero $A$. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://magazine.sebastianraschka.com/p/lora-and-dora-from-scratch) and [2](https://magazine.sebastianraschka.com/p/practical-tips-for-finetuning-llms).
